title: About page's GitHub and Documentation links are placeholders that 404 / do not resolve
what_happened: Settings > About offers three link buttons: GitHub, Documentation, Discord. GitHub opens https://github.com/skotiq-astro, which returns HTTP 404 -- the real project repo is https://github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq (HTTP 200, per the repo README badge). Documentation opens https://skotiq.astro/docs; 'skotiq.astro' does not resolve in DNS at all (.astro is not a delegated TLD). Discord opens https://discord.gg/skotiq, which is not a Skotiq invite. Clicking GitHub in the app produced no error banner -- the launch is reported as successful and the user is dropped on a 404.
expected: The three community links a shipped app puts on its About page must point at the real destinations: github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq, the docs (docs/index.md is what the README points at), and a real Discord invite -- or the button should not exist.
repro: gear icon > Settings > About > click GitHub. Then: curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404; getent hosts skotiq.astro -> no answer.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-15.png (the three buttons rendered). curl: github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404, github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq -> 200, skotiq.astro -> DNS FAILS.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/about_settings.dart:102,109,116 (and the mobile duplicates at :102/:109/:116 vs desktop :128/:135/:142)

title: Paired devices live in ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db -- outside the app database, outside the configured data dir, and split across two stores
what_happened: I launched a completely fresh scratch profile (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-system/data, --fresh, empty skotiq.db). Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing immediately listed 12 devices paired 6/15/2026 and 7/20/2026 -- the developer's real, months-old pairings. They are not in skotiq.db; PairingDatabase opens getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/pairing.db, i.e. ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db, which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely. Two such stores exist on this machine: ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db (12 active rows, mtime Aug 1) and ~/Skotiq/pairing.db (0 rows, mtime Jul 29) -- the same install has written to two different locations depending on how getApplicationDocumentsDirectory resolved.
expected: Long-lived remote credentials belong in the app database (or at minimum under the configured data dir) so that (a) Backup & Restore captures them, (b) moving the data directory moves them, (c) they cannot silently fork into two stores. As shipped, restoring a backup on a new machine silently loses every pairing, and a launch context where XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR differs presents an empty device list with no error.
repro: drive_linux.py start --profile <new> --fresh (scratch data dir) > Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing. Observe 12 devices. sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/data/skotiq.db '.tables' -> no pairing tables. sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) from paired_devices where is_active=1' -> 12, matching the UI exactly. ls ~/Skotiq/pairing.db -> a second, empty store.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-22.png (12 devices in a fresh profile). UI count 12 == DB is_active count 12. Device names/dates match row-for-row (Dashboard 2026-06-15, Android companion 2026-07-20 x3...).
where: packages/skotiq_remote_protocol/lib/src/database/pairing_database.dart:401-410 (_openConnection -> getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/pairing.db)

title: A profile saved without optics can never be edited again: Save is rejected because of the 0 the app itself stored, and the rejection is invisible on screen
what_happened: New Profile writes focal_length=0.0 / aperture=0.0. Re-open that profile, press Edit, change ONLY the name, press Save: nothing happens. No banner, no field-level error, no colour change -- the button appears dead. I clicked Save five times over three minutes and the DB never changed (still 'Backup Test Rig' while the field read 'Local Work Do Not Lose'). The failure is real and has a message -- the accessibility tree at that moment contains 'Focal length must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' and 'Aperture must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' -- but a full-window screenshot taken between the click and that tree read shows no such text anywhere on screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png), and neither does a full-resolution capture of the bottom 160px where the snackbar would sit (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-snack-1.png). The snackbar is rendered underneath the persistent bottom status bar. Clearing both optics fields let the save through -- and it stored 0.0 again, so the profile is right back in the unsavable state next time.
expected: Blank optics must round-trip as blank/NULL, not as 0.0 that the validator then rejects; and a rejected save must show its reason where the user is looking (inline under the offending field, plus a visible banner). As shipped, the very first thing a user does after creating a profile -- open it and fill something in -- hits a dead Save button with no explanation.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile > name 'X' > Create. Overflow menu > Edit > change the name > Save. Nothing happens; sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select name,focal_length,aperture from equipment_profiles' still shows the old name and 0.0/0.0. Now clear Focal Length and Aperture and press Save: it saves, and stores 0.0/0.0 again.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-64.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png (identical -- edit form with 'Local Work Do Not Lose' typed, Focal Length 0, Aperture 0, no error visible) taken immediately after the Save click; tree read after that same click contains the two validation strings; DB unchanged across all attempts.
where: validator: ProfileValidator.parseOptional... (focal/aperture 'must be a positive number') reached from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_details.dart:175-200; the empty-field -> 0.0 write is in the same save path; the snackbar is shown by the settings scaffold underneath the app's bottom status bar.

title: Backups are written to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups regardless of the configured data directory, so bundles from different databases pile into one undifferentiated 'Recent Backups' list
what_happened: I launched a brand-new scratch profile with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-system/data and an empty skotiq.db. Settings > Backup & Restore immediately listed 8 'Recent Backups' dated Aug 1 -- the developer's real bundles -- and reported 'Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 10:27'. The backup directory is ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups and ignores the data-dir override entirely, so this sandboxed instance also *wrote* into it: skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-37, -27-44, -27-45 and -30-25 are snapshots of my throwaway database (the 10:30 one records profilesCount: 0, taken right after I deleted every profile) sitting in the same list as the real ones. Nothing in the row -- name, size, date, icon -- says which database a bundle came from. A user with two installs, or anyone who has ever moved their data directory, is one click away from restoring a foreign configuration over their live one. As with pairing.db there are also two directories on this machine (~/Documents/Skotiq/backups with 9 bundles and ~/Skotiq/backups with 4), i.e. the same install has written backups to two places.
expected: Backups belong under the configured data directory, and each row should show what it contains (profiles/sequences/targets counts are already in the bundle metadata) and which install/machine wrote it. The bundle already carries appVersion and platform; add a database/install id and show it.
repro: drive_linux.py start --profile <new> --fresh > Settings > Backup & Restore. The list is non-empty on a first-ever launch. ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups -> the same 8 files, plus new skotiq_autosave_* written by the sandbox. python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('.../skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-30-25.892145.nsbackup'))['metadata'])" -> profilesCount 0, i.e. my scratch DB.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-59.png (Recent Backups list mixing Aug 1 and Aug 2 bundles). Directory listing of ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups and ~/Skotiq/backups. Bundle metadata quoted above.
where: the backup service's directory resolution (getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups) rather than the SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware resolver used by skotiq.db

title: Restore silently drops a backed-up equipment profile when its row id is already taken, and still reports 'Restored 123 items'
what_happened: The bundle skotiq_backup_2026-08-02T10-43-32.295333.nsbackup contains exactly one equipment profile: {"id": 3, "name": "Backup Test Rig"} (metadata: settingsCount 122, profilesCount 1 -> 123 items). Locally, row id 3 existed but had been renamed to 'Local Work Do Not Lose'. I restored that bundle. The toast said 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' The DB afterwards: 3|Local Work Do Not Lose|1 -- one profile, the local one, unchanged. 'Backup Test Rig' was neither inserted nor applied over row 3; it was dropped on the floor. The same restore into a database where id 3 was free DID bring the profile back (I verified that first, after deleting every row), so the discriminator is the id collision, not the bundle. The count in the message is the bundle's item count, not the number of items actually applied, so it is a claim the app has not checked.
expected: Restore must not key library items on the backup's row ids -- ids are local and get reused as soon as you delete the highest row. Re-key on content (name) or insert with a fresh id, and report what was actually written ('122 settings updated, 1 profile added, 0 skipped'), never the bundle's own count.
repro: Create a profile, Create Backup, rename that profile (or delete it and create another that takes the same rowid), then restore the bundle from Recent Backups. Toast claims all items restored; sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' shows the backed-up profile is absent.
evidence: Bundle JSON equipmentProfiles[0] = id 3 / 'Backup Test Rig'; DB after restore = 3|Local Work Do Not Lose|1; tree after restore = 'panel: Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' Control case: with equipment_profiles emptied, the same bundle restored the profile back as id 3.
where: the restore path in the backup service (row-id-keyed upsert/ignore for equipmentProfiles) called from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart

title: Every Settings snackbar renders underneath the persistent bottom status bar, so all success and failure feedback in Settings is invisible
what_happened: Four separate Settings actions produce a SnackBar that exists in the widget tree but never appears on screen, because the Settings scaffold's snackbar is drawn at the bottom of the body while the app's always-on status bar (Idle | profile | Camera Disconnected | ... | LST) is painted on top of it. Confirmed cases: (1) a rejected profile Save -- tree contains 'Focal length must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' while the full-window capture /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png shows nothing; (2) a failed catalog download -- tree contains 'Download failed: Exception: Annotation catalog download failed' while a full-resolution capture of the bottom 200px at the same moment (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-75.png) shows only the status bar; (3) 'Failed to save profile: Exception: Profile not found'; (4) 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' In every case I captured the screen between the click and a tree read that still contained the message, so the message was live and not yet dismissed. The user's experience is a button that does nothing, for both failures and successes.
expected: Feedback must be visible. Either give the SnackBar a bottom margin equal to the status-bar height (Flutter: SnackBarBehavior.floating with margin), or host it above the status bar in the shell.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile > Edit > rename > Save (rejected). Or Settings > Catalogs > Download Standard (~50 MB) (VizieR TAP currently 503). Take a screenshot immediately; nothing is shown. Then run drive_linux.py tree and find the message text in the accessibility tree.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-75.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-snack-1.png -- all captured while the corresponding message was present in the accessibility tree.
where: the ScaffoldMessenger used by packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/* vs the persistent status bar in the desktop shell

title: Remote Access claims 'Localhost stays frictionless for this machine' -- localhost is not exempt from auth at all
what_happened: With Enable Remote Access on, the page's footer note reads 'Localhost stays frictionless for this machine, while non-local clients must pair before they can control the app', the 'Open on this computer' card says 'Use this link from the same machine to confirm the dashboard is working before sharing it elsewhere', and Connection details reports Authentication = 'Paired devices required remotely'. All three say local is special. It is not: from 127.0.0.1, GET /api/status -> 401 {'error':'Authentication required','message':'Missing Authorization header or session cookie'}; so do /api/images/recent, /api/auth/csrf and POST /api/auth/cookie. The bytes returned to 127.0.0.1 and to 192.168.1.20 are identical 401s. Only the static /dashboard shell is 200, and it can load no data. The auth middleware has no loopback branch at all.
expected: Either implement the documented loopback exemption (peer address is loopback -> full-scope identity), or change the copy so it does not promise a local escape hatch that does not exist. As written, an operator clicking 'Open Local Dashboard' to 'confirm the dashboard is working' sees a dead page and concludes the server is broken.
repro: Settings > Remote Access > Enable Remote Access. Then: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/status -> 401. curl http://localhost:<port>/api/status -> 401. curl http://192.168.1.20:<port>/api/status -> 401.
evidence: Live 401 bodies captured from 127.0.0.1:8080 and 127.0.0.1:8099 (both ports I ran on). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-20.png shows the 'Open on this computer' copy, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-19.png shows Connection details.
where: copy: packages/skotiq_app/lib/localization/skotiq_localizations/translations.dart:389 and :399; enforcement: apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart:758-770 (token==null -> 401, no peer-address check anywhere in the chain).

title: After a device pairs successfully the desktop keeps showing the pairing code counting down, and the device list does not update
what_happened: I pressed Start Pairing Mode, read the code ASTRO-NEBULA-1815 off the screen, and completed pairing over HTTP (POST /api/pairing/verify -> 200 with a bearer token). The server immediately invalidated the code (a second verify with the same code returned invalid_pairing_code) and wrote the 13th row into paired_devices. The desktop screen did not react at all: 30s later it still displayed 'Enter this code on your device: ASTRO-NEBULA-1815 / Expires in 04:18 / Cancel Pairing', and Paired Devices still listed 12 entries. Only after manually pressing the small refresh icon did the 13th device appear.
expected: The instant a code is consumed the panel should close and announce which device paired -- that confirmation is the operator's only way to know the phone in their hand is the device that just connected. Showing a live countdown for a code the server has already destroyed is a false statement, and it invites the operator to read the dead code to a second device.
repro: Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing > Start Pairing Mode. From a shell: curl -X POST -d '{"code":"<code>","deviceName":"x","deviceId":"x","deviceType":"browser"}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/pairing/verify. Watch the desktop: unchanged. sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) from paired_devices where is_active=1' -> 13 while the UI shows 12.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-23.png (code panel), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-24.png (still counting down at 04:03 after the pair completed). Tree: 12 'Paired:' rows vs DB 13. After pressing refresh: 13 rows, 'audit-probe ... Paired: 1m ago'.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/pairing_screen.dart:96/215 (loadPairedDevices is only called on init and on the manual refresh button; nothing subscribes to pairing completion).

title: Paired devices always say 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet' -- last_connected_at is never written
what_happened: Every one of the 13 paired devices shows the badge 'Not seen yet' and the line 'No connection recorded yet'. I proved this is untrue for at least one of them: after pairing 'audit-probe' I made three authenticated GET /api/status calls with its bearer (200, 200, 200) and then opened an authenticated WebSocket to /events (HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols, held open 60s). paired_devices.last_connected_at for that device stayed NULL and the UI still says 'Not seen yet'. All 12 pre-existing devices -- including ones that demonstrably drove this app in earlier sessions ('ui-audit-avd', 'Lead Harness') -- are likewise NULL.
expected: last_connected_at should be stamped whenever a device authenticates. Without it the operator cannot tell a phone that is still in use from a stale credential, which makes the revoke list unusable: 7 of the 13 rows are named 'Android companion' with identical subtitles and no last-seen, IP or model to tell them apart.
repro: Pair a device via POST /api/pairing/verify, call GET /api/status with the returned bearer (200), then sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db "select device_name,last_connected_at from paired_devices where device_id='audit-probe-rss'" -> last_connected_at empty. Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing > refresh: row still reads 'No connection recorded yet'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-24.png (every row 'Not seen yet'); SQL output showing NULL last_connected_at for all 13 rows; curl 200s and the 101 upgrade transcript.
where: packages/skotiq_remote_protocol/lib/src/database/pairing_database.dart (no update of last_connected_at on the auth path) / apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart token resolution.

title: 'Active Viewers' on the Remote Access page counts co-imaging collaborators, not connected remote clients -- it stays 0 with a live dashboard socket open
what_happened: Connection details is introduced as 'Open this section when you need viewer counts, authentication state, or the last runtime error' and shows 'Active Viewers'. evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-28.png ('Active Viewers 0') captured while ss showed the ESTAB pair on :8099 and the probe had logged '101 Switching Protocols'.

title: Filter Focus Offsets silently omits the filter you just added -- you cannot set an offset for it without saving and re-opening the editor
what_happened: In Settings > Equipment Profiles > (profile) > Edit, I added a 4th filter 'SII' with the + button and typed its name. title: Deleting your last equipment profile leaves a ghost profile on screen whose 'Set Active' throws an unhandled exception and does nothing
what_happened: Settings > Equipment Profiles with exactly one profile ('Audit Rig Alpha'): overflow > Delete > Delete. equipment_profiles goes to 0 rows and the list column correctly reads 'No profiles yet' -- but the detail pane on the right keeps rendering the deleted profile in full (name, f/8.0, gain 100, all four filters, focus offsets) with a live 'Set Active' button and a live overflow menu. title: Backup & Restore contradicts itself about what restore does -- one card says nothing is merged, the confirm dialog says nothing is deleted
what_happened: The Backup & Sync card states: 'Sync is bundle-based: restoring replaces local configuration - nothing is merged.' The restore confirmation on the same screen states the opposite: 'This imports "<file>" without deleting your current data. Settings with the same keys may be updated, and library items from the backup may be added.' I measured which is true for the local path: I inserted app_settings key 'audit_canary'='present' (not in the bundle), deleted every equipment profile, then restored the bundle. Result: the profile came back AND audit_canary was still 'present' -- merge semantics. So the Backup & Sync sentence is the false one, and it is the more dangerous direction to be wrong in: a user who believes 'replaces local configuration' will restore expecting a clean slate and instead get a hybrid of two configurations with no way to tell which settings came from where.
expected: One sentence, true for both the local and the remote path, and a restore that states exactly what it will do to each category (settings overwritten by key, library items added, nothing removed).
repro: Settings > Backup & Restore. Read the Backup & Sync paragraph. Click the restore icon on any Recent Backups row and read the dialog. Then: sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db "insert into app_settings values('audit_canary','present')"; delete from equipment_profiles; restore the bundle; both the profile and audit_canary are present afterwards.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-58.png (the 'nothing is merged' paragraph) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-60.png (the 'without deleting your current data' dialog). SQL before/after quoted above.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart (Backup & Sync description vs the restore confirm dialog copy)

title: GLADE+ catalog download is broken end to end: the VizieR TAP endpoint it targets returns 503, and the app's only report of that is a snackbar you cannot see
what_happened: Settings > Catalogs > GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog > 'Download Standard (~50 MB)': the button flips to 'Downloading...' for about 3 seconds, then silently returns to its idle label. glade_plus_galaxies.csv stays 0 bytes and no .partial appears. Only the accessibility tree carries the reason -- 'Download failed: Exception: Annotation catalog download failed' -- and that snackbar is hidden behind the status bar (see the snackbar finding), so on screen the button simply does nothing. The cause is upstream: the URL built by buildGladePlusUrl() targets https://tapvizier.cds.unistra.fr/TAPVizieR/tap/sync, and I reproduced the exact query with curl -- HTTP 503 'No server is available to handle this request' in 0.36 s, while https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/ itself answers 200. So the one deep-sky catalog the app offers to fetch on demand cannot be fetched at all, on any tier.
expected: A download that cannot succeed should say so in plain language and name the host ('VizieR TAP is not responding (HTTP 503) - try again later, or use Import from File'), and the app should not depend on a single TAP mirror for a 2 GB optional catalog.
repro: Settings > Catalogs > scroll to GLADE+ > Download Standard (~50 MB). title: The desktop app can never tell you a new version exists: the only 'Updates' page in Settings is for a remote appliance, and the built-in update manager is wired to a server URL nothing ever sets
what_happened: Searching Settings for 'update' returns exactly two entries: About and 'Appliance Updates'. Appliance Updates says 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its updates. The local desktop app updates itself through its own installer.' and renders nothing else off-network. There is no local update check anywhere in Settings, and About (which the settings catalog even tags with the keyword 'updates') shows only a version string and three web links. The app does ship an in-app updater -- app.dart:204-206 wraps the desktop shell in UpdateManagerWidget, which fires _checkForUpdates() 3 s after launch -- but that check is gated on state.updateServerUrl being non-empty (update_manager_widget.dart:40-43) and the only caller of UpdateNotifier.configure(serverUrl:) in the whole repo is apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/update_wiring.dart, i.e. the appliance server, never the GUI. So on the shipped desktop build the updater is inert: I ran the app for ~40 minutes with working internet and it made no version request, showed no update UI, and logged nothing about updates. The sentence 'updates itself through its own installer' is also not true of the Linux build, which is distributed as a tarball with no installer.
expected: A 'Check for updates' row in About or a Software Update section: current version + build, channel (stable/beta), last checked, and a manual check. NINA and SGP both check at launch and show release notes; an astrophotographer needs to know a fix landed before the night, not after.
repro: Settings > search 'update' -> About, Appliance Updates. Open Appliance Updates on the desktop build: one explanatory sentence, no controls. Open About: version 6.1.0, three links, System Information. No update control anywhere. drive_linux.py log over the whole session contains no update/version request.
evidence: tree of Settings > Appliance Updates (title, subtitle 'Check for, stage, and apply updates to the connected rig', single info panel). Source: packages/skotiq_app/lib/app.dart:204-206, packages/skotiq_updater/lib/src/widgets/update_manager_widget.dart:40-52, packages/skotiq_updater/lib/src/services/update_service.dart:236-239 ('Update server URL not configured'), and grep showing update_wiring.dart:79 as the sole configure() caller.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/update_settings.dart (appliance-only page) and the unconfigured desktop path above

what_happened: Settings > Logs is the surface a user is told to use ('View application logs with filtering and export'). The level filter reports the whole session as one error: Error+ = '1 of 139 entries', the single [ProfileActivationWriteThrough] 'Strict activation aborted: target profile 1 does not exist'. title: Duplicate reports 'Duplicate profile failed' for a duplicate that succeeded, and leaks an internal invariant message to the user
what_happened: Settings > Equipment Profiles > (profile) > Duplicate > Duplicate, accepting the pre-filled name. The app reported: 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 5 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' The duplicate had in fact succeeded -- equipment_profiles gained row 5 and the profile list in the same screen shows it (three rows: 'Local Work Do Not Lose' [Active], 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)', 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)'). So the message is false in both halves: the operation did not fail, and profile 5 is not absent from the list. It reads like a post-write assertion racing the provider refresh, and the assertion text -- which names a row id and an internal list -- is shown verbatim to the user.
expected: Report success, or if the refresh really has not landed, retry/await it rather than declaring failure. A user who believes this message will press Duplicate again and end up with a third copy.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > select a profile > overflow > Duplicate > press Duplicate. (I hit it on the second duplicate of the same source profile, i.e. when the proposed name collided with an existing profile.) sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' shows the new row; the list in the UI shows it too.
evidence: tree: 'panel: Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 5 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' alongside DB rows 3,4,5 and a list rendering all three.
where: the duplicate handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_controls.dart and the profiles notifier's post-duplicate lookup

title: Duplicate happily creates two profiles with byte-identical names, while Import de-duplicates -- so the profile list can show rows nothing can tell apart
what_happened: Duplicating the same profile twice and accepting the offered name both times produced ids 4 and 5, both named 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)'. The list renders two identical rows (same title, same 'No description', same icon) with nothing to distinguish them, and the status-bar profile chip shows only a name, so once one of them is active you cannot tell which. The importer, by contrast, does resolve collisions -- importing a profile named 'Audit Rig Alpha' over an existing one produced 'Audit Rig Alpha (1)'. Two code paths, two different rules.

title: The 'default startup profile' that Settings > General promises has no UI anywhere -- it is pinned to whichever profile you created first
what_happened: Settings > General > Auto-connect equipment reads 'Connects the default startup profile on launch, falling back to the last active profile when no default is set'. Equipment Profiles has no notion of a default: the badge says 'Active', the header action says 'Set Active', and the overflow menu is Edit / Duplicate / Export / Delete. Nothing shows or sets a default. In the database equipment_profiles.is_default is set on whichever profile was created first and never moves: after I created a profile (is_default=1), duplicated it twice (both is_default=0) and pressed Set Active on a duplicate, the rows read 3|...|is_active=0|is_default=1, 4|...|is_active=1|is_default=0. So the rig the app says it will connect on launch is not the rig the operator just made active, and there is no screen where that can be seen, let alone changed.
expected: Either show and let the user set the default (a 'Set as default startup profile' item in the overflow, and a 'Default' badge in the list), or drop the concept and make auto-connect use the active profile -- which is what the operator will assume.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > create a profile, duplicate it, select the copy and press Set Active. sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name,is_active,is_default from equipment_profiles' -> is_default is still on the original. Search all of Settings for 'default profile': the only hit is the General page's description text.
evidence: DB rows quoted above; Equipment Profiles tree showing only 'Active' / 'Set Active' and the four-item overflow menu; General settings copy captured in the tree.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/ (no default affordance) vs the auto-connect description in the general settings section
